conclusions.text: Eighteen indexed records report the order that Abū Bakr lead the prayer during the final illness. They come through five Companions: ʿĀʾisha (12), Abū Mūsā (3), and Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās and Sālim b. ʿUbayd (1 each). Every route through ʿĀʾisha ends with her.
Every member affirms the order itself ("murū Abā Bakr"). No member negates it.

The objection is worded three ways: "rajul asīf" (al-Aʿmash → Ibrāhīm → al-Aswad and Saʿd b. Ibrāhīm → ʿUrwa), "rajul raqīq" (Abū Mūsā, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās routes), and "he will not make the people hear for weeping" (Hishām b. ʿUrwa → ʿUrwa). These are classed as wording variants of one objection.

Only ʿĀʾisha’s report via Ḥamza b. ʿAbd Allāh (Muslim 418e) states her motive: she feared people would see an ill omen in whoever first stood in his place. The rest are silent on this, which is an omission, not a contradiction.
Who supported him to the mosque: Ibn ʿAbbās (Ibn Mājah 1235) names al-ʿAbbās and ʿAlī. The ʿĀʾisha reports in this set say "between two men" without naming them, so there is no conflict.

uncertainties: Muwaṭṭaʾ Mālik record 100906 (stored no. 418) could not be matched to a sunnah.com page yet. Every stored Muwaṭṭaʾ link uses the form sunnah.com/malik:N, which returns 404. It stays an unverified candidate.
All 18 stored numbers/links differ from the sunnah.com reference (for example Bukhārī 646 → 664, Muslim 843 → 418f, Ibn Mājah 966 → 1232).
Isnad names are auto-extracted text chunks (candidates). Single-report branches show the collector’s teacher as their "common link", which is trivially true and carries no weight.
Riyāḍ al-Ṣāliḥīn 1670 was excluded because it is a derivative quotation.
Narrative group 17 (age at death) is a different question and is not merged. No existing narrative group covers this incident.
